standard.title: Relationships in Graphs
standard.description: describe relationships between variables represented in graphs of functions from authentic data
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can locate points in all four quadrants of the Cartesian plane and describe coordinate changes (from AC9M6SP02). Students understand dependent and independent variables in patterns.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students describe relationships between variables in graphs from authentic data, identifying key features and interpreting what the graph communicates about the relationship.

nodes.label: Reading and interpreting graphs of real data
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students read values from graphs of authentic data and describe what the graph shows in context.
nodes.minimum_width: Read specific values from a graph and describe the overall trend in plain language.
nodes.typical_width: Identify increases, decreases, peaks, plateaus, and interpret what these mean in the context of the data (e.g. energy usage, stock value).
wider: Investigate travel graphs: identify periods of travel, stopping, and return; compute average speed from slope.
Compare two graphs representing the same phenomenon (e.g. gas vs electricity usage) and discuss what each reveals.

response_modes.reason: Interpreting a graph requires understanding the specific context of the data. Students who only practise with constructed graphs often fail to interpret authentic messy data. Varied authentic contexts build flexible reading skills.

success_criteria: Reads specific values from a graph accurately.
Describes trends (increasing, decreasing, constant, periodic) in contextual terms.
Does not interpret a graph in isolation from its axes labels and units.

nodes.label: Identifying and describing the relationship between variables
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students identify and describe the relationship between the two variables in a graph, including direction, rate of change, and any notable features.
nodes.minimum_width: State the relationship between the two variables in a graph (e.g. 'as time increases, distance increases at a constant rate').
nodes.typical_width: Describe the relationship, rate of change, turning points, and intervals; explain what unusual features (sudden changes, plateaus) indicate in context.
wider: Compare linear and non-linear relationships in graphs from authentic data — informally describe what makes one 'linear looking'.
Tell the 'story' behind a graph of a function: describe what events might explain the shape (e.g. a graph representing water level in a bathtub).

response_modes.reason: Relating graph shape to contextual events (the 'story' behind a graph) requires experiencing many different authentic contexts. Students who only describe slope fail to interpret contextual meaning.

success_criteria: Describes the relationship between variables including direction and approximate rate of change.
Identifies and interprets at least one notable feature (e.g. peak, plateau, sudden change) in context.
Uses the variable names from the axes in their description.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Authentic data graphs offer rich comparative and narrative opportunities — advancing students can move from describing to explaining the story behind the shape, including non-linear patterns.
